monitor_list.name: Visayas/Mindanao regasification facility (unnamed, conceptual)
monitor_list.sponsor: unnamed; DOE official (Sec./Usec. Garin) floated the idea publicly
monitor_list.why_below_threshold: No named sponsor/developer, no site, no concrete project step -- purely a DOE official's stated future option ('eventually we may put a regasification facility somewhere in Visayas or Mindanao'). Fails (a) and (c) of the tight threshold. Also contradicted by an October 2025 BusinessWorld report that the Philippines is unlikely to add any new LNG terminal near-term because existing terminals run at only ~60% of regasification capacity.

notes: Cross-checked DOE's full roster of DOE-approved/NTP LNG projects (the widely-cited 'seven approved LNG projects': AG&P/Linseed (Ilijan/Batangas), First Gen (Tabangao/FGEN Batangas FSRU), Excelerate (Filipinas LNG Gateway/Luzon LNG), Energy World (Pagbilao), Vires Energy Corp, Shell Energy Philippines (Tabangao), and Samat LNG Corp (Mariveles)) against the 14-terminal covered list. All seven map 1:1 onto covered GEM records -- no unmapped DOE-approved project found. Also checked for any newer/eighth DOE-approved project post-2023 and found none in trade press. The one notable 2024-2025 development (Meralco PowerGen / Aboitiz Power / San Miguel Global Power $3.3bn joint venture) is a change-of-control/expansion of the EXISTING AG&P/Linseed Ilijan terminal, not a new site -- flagged here for awareness but this is Update-workflow territory (ownership/operator change on a covered terminal), not a Discovery finding. Searched specifically for Visayas/Mindanao regas proposals (a DOE official floated the idea in interviews) and found no named sponsor or site -- placed in monitor_list, well below the tight threshold, and further undercut by an Oct 2025 BusinessWorld report that the Philippines is unlikely to build any new LNG terminal near-term given existing terminals run at only ~60% utilization. No gem.wiki-only pages, no domestic-only/out-of-scope plants, and no dormant-site revivals were found distinct from the 14 covered records.
summary: No new Philippine LNG terminal meeting the tight discovery threshold was found across Ring A (DOE/regulatory) and Ring B (trade press) sources for 2023-2026. Every currently active or DOE-approved LNG project in the Philippines -- AG&P/Linseed Field (Ilijan/Batangas), Excelerate/Filipinas LNG Gateway (Luzon LNG), Energy World (Pagbilao), Vires Energy Corp, Shell Energy Philippines (Tabangao), and Samat LNG Corp (Mariveles) -- maps directly onto one of the 14 terminals already covered in GEM's tracker; none is a genuinely distinct new site or sponsor. The one live 2024-2025 development, a $3.3bn Meralco PowerGen/Aboitiz Power/San Miguel Global Power joint-venture acquisition of the existing AG&P/Linseed Ilijan terminal, is an ownership change on a covered terminal (Update-workflow territory), not a new terminal. A vague DOE-official mention of a possible future Visayas/Mindanao regasification site has no named sponsor, location, or concrete step and is listed only in the monitor list; an October 2025 BusinessWorld report additionally notes the Philippines is unlikely to add new LNG terminal capacity near-term given only ~60% utilization of existing terminals. No candidates, no out-of-scope finds, and no gem.wiki-only pages were identified.
